recognize_zh: AIDS 患者的血液抹片中，中性球（A）與單核球／巨噬細胞（B）的細胞質內塞滿許多 2–4 µm 的小型卵圓形酵母菌，每個有偏心新月形的染色質與周圍透明暈（pseudocapsule），符合播散性組織漿菌症（disseminated histoplasmosis）。
features: Numerous small (2-4 µm) oval intracellular yeasts within neutrophils (panel A) and a monocyte/macrophage (panel B)
Each yeast has an eccentric crescent of dark-staining chromatin
No budding on broad bases or hyphae visible; organisms are uniform in size
A few extracellular yeasts adjacent to the ruptured/host cell; background leukocytes and red cells
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows neutrophils and a monocyte/macrophage containing numerous small, uniform oval yeast forms measuring approximately 2-4 µm. Each organism has an eccentric crescent-shaped chromatin mass and a surrounding clear halo (pseudocapsule), and some lie extracellularly adjacent to the host cell. No hyphae or pseudohyphae are identified. In a severely immunosuppressed patient with pancytopenia and hepatosplenomegaly, findings are consistent with disseminated Histoplasma capsulatum infection; fungal culture, GMS/PAS stains, and urine antigen testing are recommended.

ddx.vs: Talaromyces yeasts are similar in size but divide by fission with a central transverse septum and are elongated or sausage-shaped rather than budding oval forms.
Leishmania amastigotes contain a distinct rod-shaped kinetoplast next to the nucleus and lack a clear pseudocapsular halo.
Candida yeasts are larger (3-6 µm), stain more deeply without a halo, and often show budding with pseudohyphae.
Toxoplasma tachyzoites are crescentic with central nuclei, while Cryptococcus is larger (4-10 µm) with a thick mucicarmine-positive capsule and narrow-based budding.
